title: Token-economics attribution service for per-route/model/customer breakdowns
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a scalable backend service that computes per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency attributions based on token usage and runtime telemetry. The service will produce time-windowed rollups and fine-grained attributions that the Console uses for per-route dashboards, customer billing previews, and internal cost analysis. Unlike previous rollups, this service accounts for: model variants (float vs quantized), prefix/KV cache hit adjustments, streaming partial responses, and multi-stage pipelines (generation -> rerank -> embed). It must support incremental computation, backfills, and deterministic reconciliation with authoritative billing sources.
acceptance_criteria: Service produces hourly and daily rollups for token cost and P95 latency per route, model, and customer
Attribution accounts for model-specific cost multipliers and cache-hit discounts and exposes both raw and normalized token counts
Computed metrics reconcile (within 0.5%) with the canonical billing rollup in canonical/billing dataset for a 7-day test window
API exposes query endpoints for ad-hoc ranges and pre-computed time series consumed by Console UI
Backfill job can recompute arbitrary day ranges and will autoslice to avoid OOM on high-cardinality days
Schema and computed fields documented and added to console data catalog with examples
technical_notes: Ingest sources: request logs (edge), runtime telemetry (per-token timing), model catalog (cost multipliers), cache-proxy hits, and streaming partial events
Primary computation is a rolling aggregation keyed by (customer_id, route_id, model_id, variant, hour). Use time-based sharding (YYYYMMDDHH) and sticky job workers to reduce cross-shard joins
Token attribution: derive effective token charge = tokens_generated + tokens_consumed_by_tools + (1 - cache_hit_rate) * prefix_tokens where applicable
Latency attribution: compute per-request latency and incremental per-token latencies; maintain reservoir summaries for P50/P95/P99 across windows
Cost model: apply model-specific GPU multiplier and hardware region factor. Keep an extensible multiplier table in config; support overrides per-customer for Dedicated pricing
Windowing: use tumbling hourly windows for rollups and an additional daily aggregator that compacts hourly buckets into day partitions
Fault tolerance: use Kafka topics with compacted model metadata and exactly-once consumers where possible; idempotent writes to rollup store (BigQuery or ClickHouse) using dedupe by event_id
Backfills: orchestration via batch workers with exponential slice sizing (start with 1-hour slices, double until max 24h), and job checkpoints in metadata store

Query patterns: Console UI needs per-route time series for last 7/30/90 days and ad-hoc breakdowns by model variant and region. Provide pre-aggregated materialized views to keep interactive latency <300ms
Operational metrics: ingestion lag, compute lag, job retry counts, distinct cardinality growth, tail memory usage. Add alerts for >15m ingestion lag or >2x expected hourly cost delta

implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype consumer, hourly aggregator, materialized hourly table, basic Console API endpoints (3 weeks)
Phase 2: Add cache-aware attribution, model multipliers, and reconciliation job (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Backfill tooling, daily compaction, performance tuning and On-Call runbook (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Add embeddings/rerank attribution and tenant override table; GA and migration plan for Console dashboards (2 weeks)
